summary: The most probable root cause is the 14:10 redis-cache config change (maxmemory 4gb to 1gb, allkeys-lru). Memory hit its 97% ceiling and mass eviction began (first logged 14:10:35, 12000 keys per batch from 14:11:05). Order-router's first 'idempotency key not found for retried webhook, treating as new order' warning followed at 14:11:11, and duplicate_orders first became non-zero in the 14:10 bucket. The link is timing-based: no log or metric shows that dedup or idempotency keys were actually among the evicted keys, so the mechanism is an inference. The 14:02 order-router deploy and a WhatsApp provider re-send remain unexcluded, but neither has direct support. Treat the deploy as a possible co-contributor to check, not a confirmed cause.

hypotheses.statement: The 14:10 redis-cache config change (maxmemory 4gb to 1gb, allkeys-lru) drove memory to its 97% ceiling and mass eviction, which removed order-router idempotency/dedup keys before retried webhooks arrived, so retries were treated as new orders and executed twice.
hypotheses.label: medium

supporting.text: A redis-cache config change at 14:10 cut maxmemory from 4gb to 1gb and set allkeys-lru, exactly at incident onset.
Eviction began inside the 14:10 minute (evicted_keys 0 at 14:09, 6000 at 14:10, 12000 per minute from 14:11). Memory rose from 60% to 97% and stayed at the ceiling.
The first eviction warning (14:10:35) came 36 seconds before, and the 12000-key batch (14:11:05) six seconds before, order-router's first idempotency miss at 14:11:11.
Order-router calls redis-cache synchronously, so the eviction sits on its request path.

contradicting.text: Nothing shows that evicted keys were dedup or idempotency keys. Eviction logs do not name keys and no key schema or TTL was queried. The mechanism is assumed. It is likely that cold, write-once dedup keys were LRU candidates, but this is unverified.
Aggregate redis hit_ratio barely moved (0.942 at 14:11, versus a pre-incident low of 0.928). The dip is within baseline variation and cannot isolate idempotency lookups.

Counts do not reconcile. The metric plateaus at 18.0 from 14:19, while idempotency-miss warnings continue at about 3 per minute through 14:29 and later. Either the metric and logs count different things, or some misses are not duplicates. The metric's 14:10 bucket also precedes the first logged miss.
The logs do not show that WhatsApp-originated orders reach order-router. The graph shows web-app as its only caller, so the retried webhooks may come from another path.

hypotheses.statement: The 14:02 order-router dependency bump (order-router-00601) changed the redis client, key format, TTL or retry/idempotency handling, so retried webhooks stopped being deduplicated and produced duplicate orders, with the redis eviction at most a coincident trigger.
hypotheses.label: low

supporting.text: An order-router deploy (order-router-00601, 'dependency bump') landed at 14:02, about 8 minutes before onset. It was the only order-router change in the window. It is a candidate trigger only on timing, and if the bump touched the redis client, key format, TTL or retry handling, it could have caused lookup misses.

contradicting.text: duplicate_orders was 0.0 through 14:09 and became non-zero only at 14:10, which fits the redis change at 14:10 better than a deploy 8 minutes earlier.
The deploy record has only a one-line note and no diff, so what changed is unknown. Nothing in the evidence shows the bump touched dedup logic.
Logs contain no dedup-hit lines at any level for 14:00-14:11, so they cannot show whether dedup worked between the deploy and onset.

hypotheses.statement: The WhatsApp provider re-sent webhooks (receipts at 14:09:57 and 14:10:09) or inbound-msgs redelivered a message, so the same message was processed twice upstream of order-router, independent of the redis dedup store.
hypotheses.label: low

supporting.text: wa-webhook logged two 'webhook received' events 12 seconds apart (14:09:57 and 14:10:09) just before onset. The only link to retries is an assumption that they were provider re-sends, and neither line carries a message ID.

contradicting.text: The enqueue lines in wa-webhook show only distinct message IDs, so no duplicate enqueue is visible there.
No retry WARN lines appear in wa-webhook, and no rabbitmq error or latency anomaly appears, though rabbitmq has no queue-depth or redelivery series.
Orchestrator logs carry no message ID or order-submission lines, so the two receipts cannot be traced to any order.

duplicate_orders climbs by about 1.8 per minute from 14:10 and reaches 18.0 at 14:19, then stays flat at 18.0 through 14:44 (order-router)

order-router logged 'idempotency key not found' warnings through 15:09:47Z, the last line in the returned list. This is well after the duplicate_orders metric went flat at 14:19 (per E-002), so the log and metric count different things or the log is counting retries.
redis-cache eviction batch size rose to 12000 keys at 14:11:05Z, six seconds before order-router's first idempotency miss at 14:11:11Z.

redis-cache hit_ratio was 0.988 at 14:09 and 0.942 at 14:11, a small dip. The baseline already contained values as low as 0.928 at 13:56, so the change is within the pre-incident range. This is aggregate hit ratio across all redis keys, not idempotency-specific.
The WARN query returned 57 lines in total, not truncated. Counting the returned lines up to 14:19:55 gives 27, which matches the 27 in the 14:11-14:19:55 range but not the metric's 18.0 peak.

assumptions.text: Redis LRU eviction probably removed idempotency or dedup keys, so retried webhooks found no key and were created as new orders. This is consistent with the timing but unverified, because no redis key-miss or eviction count for dedup keys was queried.
The 14:10 duplicate_orders bucket (1.8) precedes the first logged idempotency miss (14:11:11Z) by about a minute. This may reflect metric bucketing or a different counting method and needs checking.
the 14:09:57 and 14:10:09 receipts could be provider re-sends that became retried webhooks, which would fit the 14:11 onset, but no shared ID links them to the order-router misses

WhatsApp-originated orders may not reach order-router at all, as the graph suggests, so the order-router duplicates may come from web-app traffic. The orchestrator logs do not reference order-router or broker-gateway, which is consistent with this but does not prove it

A dedup key is written once and read only when a retry arrives, so it looks cold to allkeys-lru and can become an eviction candidate even when written only seconds earlier. This would reconcile the eviction onset with the misses, but it is not verified: no key-level access data or LRU tail age was available.
The 14:02 deploy might have changed a redis client, serializer, key prefix, TTL or retry/idempotency library, which would let dedup lookups miss. This cannot be confirmed from any tool result.

actions.text: Revert the redis-cache config change, or raise maxmemory back toward 4gb, and watch evicted_keys and memory_pct fall and idempotency-miss warnings stop.
actions.rationale: The change coincides with eviction onset and precedes the first idempotency miss. Reverting stops eviction and tests the hypothesis directly. If misses continue after eviction stops, H2 becomes more likely.

actions.text: Identify the affected duplicate orders from broker and order records, and reconcile or cancel them with the broker and customers.
actions.rationale: duplicate_orders reached 18.0 and idempotency misses continued past the plateau, so customers may still hold duplicate executions.

actions.rationale: This is the missing link between eviction and the misses. Only timing supports it today.

actions.text: Add an idempotency-hit and miss log line or metric with message ID and caller. Make dedup keys non-evictable or store them in a durable store with a noeviction or volatile-ttl policy. Require review and a memory-headroom check for redis maxmemory and eviction policy changes.
actions.rationale: Logs cannot currently tie a miss to a message or tell whether dedup worked. An LRU policy with a 75% smaller limit can silently evict dedup state.

actions.text: Reconcile the duplicate_orders metric definition against the idempotency-miss log counts, including whether it is a cumulative counter or a capped gauge.
